# Checklists applied by the reviewer

## PRISMA 2020 (Page et al. 2021, BMJ 372:n71) — item numbers and titles
1 Title · 2 Abstract · 3 Rationale · 4 Objectives · 5 Eligibility criteria · 6 Information sources · 7 Search strategy · 8 Selection process · 9 Data collection process · 10a Outcomes, 10b Other variables · 11 Study risk of bias assessment · 12 Effect measures · 13a–f Synthesis methods · 14 Reporting bias assessment · 15 Certainty assessment · 16a–b Study selection · 17 Study characteristics · 18 Risk of bias in studies · 19 Results of individual studies · 20a–d Results of syntheses · 21 Reporting biases · 22 Certainty of evidence · 23a–d Discussion · 24a–c Registration and protocol · 25 Support · 26 Competing interests · 27 Availability of data, code and other materials.
Items 8, 9 and 11 must state that two independent agents performed the step, how agreement was measured, and that a human adjudicated.

## PRISMA-P (protocol, Gate 2)
Shamseer et al. 2015, BMJ 349:g7647 — 17 items; the search strategy for at least one database is given in full.

## PRISMA-trAIce (AI as a review tool; JMIR AI 2025, e80247)
Apply the published checklist items on: tool identity and version, stage of use, prompts and configuration, validation performed, human oversight, error handling, and limitations. Read the published item list; do not work from memory.

## Ding et al. 2026 (arXiv 2608.05179), Table 10 measured items
- Human-in-the-loop entry points stated (list of points).
- Code released (runnable repository).
- Seeds or execution traces released (re-runnable artefact).
- Novelty-verification method stated (method plus a sampled check) — for this review, the gap statement's database searches.
- Number of attempts and the selection policy stated.
The three proposed items are to be quoted from the paper's PDF before use.

## RAISE 2026 v3 (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/FWAUD) — evidence-synthesist items
Tool name, version and dates; purpose and stages affected; how it was used; justification and validation; inputs and outputs shared where feasible; human remains responsible.

## BARG (Kruschke 2021, Nat Hum Behav 5:1282–1291) — Gates 5 and 6
Priors stated and justified; prior predictive check; model specification; MCMC diagnostics (R-hat, effective sample size); posterior summaries with credible intervals; decision thresholds stated in advance; prior sensitivity; code and data available.

## ICMJE (January 2026, Section II.A.4 and Section V) — Gate 7
AI use disclosed in the cover letter and in the manuscript (methods for data collection and analysis; acknowledgments for writing assistance); no AI author; human authors responsible for all content.
====
**Stage 7, manuscript (weeks 16 to 18).** The writer agent drafts to the target journal's format with the PRISMA checklist cross-referenced; the citation agent verifies every reference a final time; the reviewer agent audits every sentence that states a number against the results package. Human authors edit in Claude Docs; the AI-use statement describes exactly which stages used which agents. Hand-over: manuscript, checklist, release package, cover letter.

**Throughout.** The monitor task, once approved at Gate 1, runs weekly: it reruns the registered search terms for new records, checks that every DOI in the master list still resolves, and posts a digest to the Project. Gate packages are stored in the Project under gate-packages with the gate number and date in the file name.

## Quality controls

Six controls run at every stage; each exists because the evidence review in this session hit the failure it guards against.

- **Dual independent work with blinding.** Screening and extraction are done twice by agents that cannot see each other's output; agreement is reported as κ or a discrepancy rate, and every conflict is adjudicated by Sean. A single agent's extraction is never final.
- **Claims-to-source audit.** The reviewer agent takes every number and quotation in a gate package and checks it against the cited page; what it cannot open is listed as unverified, never assumed. In this session the audit caught a wrong journal, a wrong year, a mislabelled guideline grade and a responder rate that was really a percentile.
- **Citation verification with pacing.** Crossref, OpenAlex and publisher pages are queried a few at a time with waits between batches, because all three rate-limited within minutes when hit in bursts; PubMed pages return no content to the fetch tool and are never used as a source. Each reference stores which route confirmed it.
- **Provenance on every datum.** The master CSV has mandatory fields for DOI or URL, location in the source, extractor, date and verification route; the analysis code refuses rows with empty provenance.
- **Fresh-session reruns.** Results are rerun by a reviewer agent that starts without the drafting context; a number that does not reproduce is a gate failure.
- **Human sign-off where journals demand it.** The GRADE table, the analysis plan and the manuscript carry a named human signature; Claude's contribution is logged for the AI-use statement.

**Known tool limits recorded for the plan.** Automated safety filters stopped two agent runs in this session when the work touched immune-challenge studies; the plan routes that extraction through the main session with Sean present rather than through background agents, and keeps the wording clinical. Publisher sites that blocked access (ahajournals, Wiley, Taylor & Francis, Science) are listed so that Sean can retrieve those papers through institutional access and stage them.

## Risks and mitigations

The risks that can sink a journal submission are listed first; each has an owner and the gate at which it is checked.

cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-chick-contact-system/9737741b-6ce5-5409-92dc-67b8f29eb2a7/scratchpad/vcr-build && cat > dry-run/DRY_RUN_PROTOCOL.md <<'EOF'
# Dry run — Gate 1 acceptance test

Plan requirement: "Dry run on five known studies reproduces the numbers already in the research document; every skill tested on one real paper."

Revised 2026-10-04 (round-2 build, fixer D) against the research document (scratchpad/inputs/docs/research-project.md; line numbers below refer to it), the reviewer's pass-2 report (section 8) and register rows R-028, R-030, R-031, R-051 to R-054 and R-064. Which five studies are chosen, and the staging of their full texts, remain Sean's decision (R-029).

## Study selection
Choose five studies that (a) are **not listed in the research document's Verification status table** (lines 164–192: the table names only the 26 of 98 sources whose figures rest partly on secondary accounts, citation records or abstracts; the document has no per-source "verified" status column, so the rule is membership in that table, not a status value), (b) have full text in hand (open access, or staged by Sean), (c) together cover the design types and appraisal tools the appraisal skill must handle (RoB 2, ROBINS-I or the `pre_post` mapping, JBI case report, JBI prevalence), and (d) are not immune-challenge studies (A09 is main-session only). Checked 2026-10-04: none of the seven candidates below appears in the Verification status table, so rule (a) excludes none of them.

Record the five chosen in dry-run/selection.csv (header shipped, no rows) before any agent runs:

`candidate, study_id, ability_id, doi, access_route, full_text_path, verification_note`

- `candidate`: the short name used in the table below. `study_id` and `ability_id`: as the screening record and skills/screening/references/abilities.md will carry them. `doi`: from the research document's reference list. `access_route` ∈ `open_access`, `pmc`, `staged_by_sean`, `institutional`. `full_text_path`: under extraction/fulltext/. `verification_note`: "not in Verification status table (research-project.md lines 168–192); checked <date>" plus anything Sean adds.

### Candidates

Targets are quoted from the research document, which is itself a pilot (charter standing condition 1); they are the reproduction test, not results. The **target type** column says whether the extractor can enter the target as printed (extraction rule 1: numbers exactly as printed, in the printed unit) or whether it is a derived quantity that analysis/01_effect_sizes.R computes from printed inputs the extractor records. Where the research document does not make clear whether a figure is printed in the paper, the row says so and the precision rule below settles it when the full text is staged.

| Candidate | Design type and tool | Target to reproduce (research document) | Target type; what the extractor records | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kozhevnikov et al. 2013, PLoS ONE (A03) [4] | non-randomised experiment (ten expert meditators; Western participants); ROBINS-I per the appraisal skill mapping, confirmed from the paper's design statement | initial core temperature 36.49 °C (SD 0.21); largest rise 2.2 °C (participant 3); highest value 38.30 °C (participant 5) (line 82) | 36.49 (SD 0.21) and 38.30 °C: **printed** (group mean and per-participant value). The 2.2 °C rise: **derived** unless the paper prints the per-participant rise; the extractor records participant 3's printed start and end-of-breathing axillary temperatures (and the group pre/post values with dispersion and n), and the rise is computed in analysis code with the derivation recorded | open access (PLoS ONE) |
| Zeidan et al. 2011, J Neurosci (A10) [72] | within-person pre/post, no sham arm, n = 15; tool per the appraisal skill's `pre_post` mapping (an SME question, R-023) | pain intensity −40% and unpleasantness −57% versus rest; intensity F(1,14) = 20.49, η² = 0.59; unpleasantness F(1,14) = 87.99, η² = 0.86 (line 128) | F and η² values: **printed**. The percentage reductions: **derived** (percent change from the rest rating) unless the paper prints the percentages; the extractor records the mean intensity and unpleasantness ratings at rest and during meditation, their dispersion type and value, and n = 15 on each row; analysis code computes the change | confirm access (J Neurosci) |
| Meissner et al. 2024, Nat Hum Behav (A08) [40] | randomised: 28 to pupil biofeedback, 28 to control (27/27 analysed), replication in 25 more; RoB 2 | group effect F(1, 21.58) = 21.49, P = 0.001, ηp² = 0.50 [0.17, 0.67]; 27/27 analysed (line 106) | **printed** (test statistic, effect size with its interval, analysed n per arm). The participant counts 56 + 25 are study characteristics, not the target. The document's d ≈ 2.0 is a conversion from ηp² (line 40) and is **derived** in analysis code, not entered by the extractor | confirm access |
| Code 1995, Percept Mot Skills (A21) [52] | prevalence survey, n = 442; JBI prevalence | about 22% could move one or the other ear, 18% both at once (line 112) | **printed as percentages** in the document; the extractor records `n_responders` and `n_tested` if the paper prints counts (PLO is computed from counts, SCHEMA); if only percentages are printed, the extractor records the percentages and n = 442 as printed and analysis code derives the counts with the derivation recorded | confirm access |
| Eberhardt et al. 2021, Int J Psychophysiol (A06) [39] | case report, one 23-year-old man, n = 1; JBI case report | from a 4.96 mm baseline, constriction by about 2.4 mm and dilation by about 0.8 mm (line 104) | 4.96 mm baseline: **printed** (line 56 carries it as the paper's own baseline). The 2.4 mm and 0.8 mm changes are given by the document as approximations ("about"): **derived** unless the paper prints the change; the extractor records the printed constricted and dilated diameters (or the printed change) with `value_source` and a precision note if read from a figure | confirm access |
| Manuck 1976, Biofeedback Self Regul (A14) [17] | 60 subjects, 15 per condition (no controls; paced breathing; chin-EMG feedback; both), 10 increase and 10 decrease trials of 60 s; **tool chosen from the paper's design statement; the research document does not state randomisation** (line 64), so "randomised, RoB 2" is not assumed — if allocation to the four conditions is stated as random, RoB 2; otherwise the appraisal skill's non-randomised mapping | mean increase +3.4 bpm; mean decrease −0.3 bpm (no decreases achieved); the size did not differ with somatic restraint (line 64) | **printed** means as the document gives them; the extractor records the condition means with dispersion and n = 15 per condition; whether the paper prints the pooled +3.4 bpm or only per-condition means is confirmed under the precision rule | confirm access |

### Screening E7 test case (not extracted, not appraised)

| Record | Role in the dry run | Expected screening result | Not a target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paravlic et al. 2018, Sports Med (A12) [49], systematic review and meta-analysis (13 studies, 370 participants; line 98) | tests the screening skill's E7-first rule on a real review record, and the head agent's reference-list mining (formerly called "harvest"; `harvest` is not a code value) at Stage 3 | `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7` from both screeners at `ta`; no `ft` stage, no extraction, no appraisal (appraisal skill: reviews are not appraised) | the pooled ES 0.72 [0.42, 1.02] is not extracted and is not a dry-run target; the comparison with the pilot value is a Stage 5 narrative point, not an extraction |

### Precision rule
Targets are quoted here at the research document's precision and are **confirmed to the papers' printed figures once the full texts are staged**: before the extractors run, the head agent (with Sean) re-reads each target in the paper, records the printed figure and its unit in dry-run/selection.csv's `verification_note` (or a per-study note in the dry-run report), and the pass criterion "reproduced as printed" refers to the paper's figure, not to this table. Known cases: the document rounds Kozhevnikov's highest value to **38.30 °C** (line 82; the evidence map's 38.3 is a further rounding); Eberhardt's **"about 2.4 mm"** and **"about 0.8 mm"** (line 104) are approximations whose printed values may differ in the last digit or be given as diameters rather than changes; Code's "about 22%" (line 112) may be printed as a count. A target that the paper prints differently from this table is corrected in the table with the line of the paper cited, before extraction, and the correction is listed in the dry-run report.

### Decoys (screening test set)
dry-run/decoys.csv holds ten out-of-scope records drawn from the research document's reference list (references [11], [13], [14], [15], [16], [77], [78], [80], [81], [82]; lines 303–308 and 369–374), chosen so that each exclusion route the screeners must handle is tested at least twice: four hardware-mediated links (E5: function not in references/abilities.md; the document's scope excludes links through implanted or external hardware, line 17), four placebo or classically conditioned responses (E2: no deliberate attempt by the person; line 17), and two meta-analyses whose subject matter would otherwise fire E5 or E2 (E7, which the screening skill tests first and which stops the sequence). Columns: `record_id, title, year, doi_or_id, expected_decision, expected_code, rationale`. Expected codes follow skills/screening/SKILL.md as revised in this round (E7 tested first, then E1–E5 in order; E8 only for an unopenable full text; E6 is the head agent's deduplication code and is never expected from a screener). The file carries titles and DOIs only; the head agent assembles the screening records file (record_id, title, abstract, year, authors, source_db, doi) from the staged record data, and the screeners decide from the record text alone. The three immune-conditioning decoys are placebo/conditioning records, not A09 immune-challenge studies; if a safety filter stops a run on one of them, the stop is recorded (trace `safety_stop_subject`; methods-paper outcome #8) and the record is replaced from the same reference list at Sean's direction.

## Procedure
1. Screening: both screener agents (A, B) screen the five selected records, the Paravlic 2018 record and the ten decoys at `ta` (16 records), then the five selected records at `ft`. The head agent compares each decision with the expected decision (decoys.csv; the five selected records are expected `include`; Paravlic `exclude`/E7) and the two screeners with each other.
2. Extraction: both extractor agents extract the five studies into separate copies of master_extraction.csv. The head agent diffs them with tools/reconcile.py; discrepancies are listed (tools/RECONCILIATION.md).
3. Appraisal: appraisal agent applies the tool selected from each paper's design statement (appraisal skill mapping; Manuck 1976 and Zeidan 2011 as noted above) to each of the five studies and drafts the GRADE row for each ability. Paravlic 2018 is not appraised.
4. Reviewer: reviewer agent, fresh session, audits the five extractions against the full texts and the targets as confirmed under the precision rule.
5. Pooling-code test (synthetic): `bash analysis/synthetic/run_synthetic_tests.sh` from the package root (fixer B's script; the five dry-run studies inform five different abilities, k = 1 each, so the real dry run never reaches pooling, leave-one-out, Egger, forest or funnel code). The script generates the synthetic masters under analysis/synthetic/ (every `study_id` starts with `synth_`, provenance fields are obviously synthetic, and nothing is written under extraction/), runs `Rscript analysis/run_all.R` on a dry-run-shaped master (five abilities, k = 1) and on a pooling master (k ≥ 3 per unit, one k = 12 unit for Egger and funnel) and asserts the contract outputs and headers. **Pass criterion: exit 0 and the asserted outputs** (the script's final line reads `== synthetic tests: 0 failure(s)`). Checked 2026-10-04 on a copy of this tree in the build environment (R 4.3.3, metafor 4.4.0, bayesmeta absent): exit 0, 51 checks ok, 0 failures; bayes_pooled.csv carries note rows because bayesmeta is absent.
6. Environment: `Rscript analysis/setup.R`; `Rscript analysis/run_all.R` on the reconciled dry-run master (five real studies). Confirm the one-command rebuild and the provenance refusal (delete one location field in a scratch copy and confirm the load stops; analysis/00_load.R writes REFUSED_*.csv).
7. Every run logged with the trace logger; every prompt stored under traces/prompts/.

## Agreement statistics and acceptance
- Screening: Cohen's κ (agent A vs agent B) at `ta` on the 16 records and at `ft` on the five, each **reported with its 95% CI**. At this size κ is reported, not used as the acceptance threshold: with 16 records whose expected split (5 include, 11 exclude) is fixed by construction, the CI of κ is wide, one disagreement moves κ substantially, and the decoys were chosen to be clear-cut, so κ measures the test's design as much as the screeners. **Acceptance criterion: every disagreement (agent vs agent, and agent vs expected decision or expected code) is listed in the dry-run report and adjudicated by Sean, with the reason.** The exclusion code is compared as well as the decision, so that a correct `exclude` with the wrong code (for example E2 or E5 recorded for a meta-analysis instead of E7) is a listed disagreement.
- Extraction: field-level exact-agreement rate and numeric discrepancy rate (tools/reconcile.py); every discrepancy listed and adjudicated.

## Access plan
Full texts are staged by Sean before the run (rule (b)); only Kozhevnikov 2013 (PLoS ONE) is open access with confirmed access today. The research document records these access failures during its own review (line 206), and the dry run expects them: **ahajournals, Wiley, Taylor & Francis, Science and gastrojournal returned 403; PubMed pages returned no content; PNAS, PMC and JAMA Network intermittently served CAPTCHAs; Europe PMC, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and ResearchGate rate-limited after a few requests.** Consequences for the dry run: agents never decide from a snippet (screening rule 5: an unopenable full text is `unsure`/E8 for Sean); API lookups are paced (plan quality control "citation verification with pacing"); each staged full text records its `access_route`; and any new failure is added to this list in the dry-run report (methods-paper outcome #8).

## Pass criteria
- Every printed target reproduced exactly as printed in the paper (precision rule), each with a complete provenance block; every derived target reproduced by analysis/01_effect_sizes.R from the extracted printed inputs, to the research document's precision, with the derivation recorded in `derivation`.
- Extractor A and B agree on every target value, or every discrepancy is explained by a documented source ambiguity and adjudicated.
- Screening: every disagreement listed and adjudicated (κ with CI reported); Paravlic 2018 excluded with E7 by both screeners; no decoy included.
- Each of the four skills executed on at least one real paper, with its trace record complete.
- Reviewer report: no open FAIL on the dry-run package.
- `bash analysis/synthetic/run_synthetic_tests.sh` exits 0 with the asserted outputs.
- run_all.R rebuilds from the reconciled master; renv.lock and session_info.txt committed (environment route per analysis/ENVIRONMENT.md and R-038).
- No agent run touched A09 material.

## Report
dry-run/DRY_RUN_REPORT_<date>.md: selection table with verification routes and the printed figures confirmed under the precision rule; per-study target vs extracted (A, B); κ with CI and the full disagreement list with adjudications; extraction discrepancy list; appraisal rows with the tool-selection rule recorded for each study; reviewer report; synthetic-test output; environment manifest; trace ids; list of what did not work and why (including access failures and any safety stop). This report is the core of gate-packages/G1_<date>_team-and-tooling.md.
EOF
echo written; wc -l dry-run/DRY_RUN_PROTOCOL.md
input.description: Write the revised dry-run protocol

The document's d ≈ 2.0 is a conversion from ηp² (line 40) and is **derived** in analysis code, not entered by the extractor | confirm access |

| Record | Role in the dry run | Expected screening result | Not a target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paravlic et al. 2018, Sports Med (A12) [49], systematic review and meta-analysis (13 studies, 370 participants; line 98) | tests the screening skill's E7-first rule on a real review record, and the head agent's reference-list mining (formerly called "harvest"; `harvest` is not a code value) at Stage 3 | `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7` from both screeners at `ta`; no `ft` stage, no extraction, no appraisal (appraisal skill: reviews are not appraised) | the pooled ES 0.72 [0.42, 1.02] is not extracted and is not a dry-run target; the comparison with the pilot value is a Stage 5 narrative point, not an extraction |

### Precision rule
Targets are quoted here at the research document's precision and are **confirmed to the papers' printed figures once the full texts are staged**: before the extractors run, the head agent (with Sean) re-reads each target in the paper, records the printed figure and its unit in dry-run/selection.csv's `verification_note` (or a per-study note in the dry-run report), and the pass criterion "reproduced as printed" refers to the paper's figure, not to this table. dry-run/decoys.csv holds ten out-of-scope records drawn from the research document's reference list (references [11], [13], [14], [15], [16], [77], [78], [80], [81], [82]; lines 303–308 and 369–374), chosen so that each exclusion route the screeners must handle is tested at least twice: four hardware-mediated links (E5: function not in references/abilities.md; the document's scope excludes links through implanted or external hardware, line 17), four placebo or classically conditioned responses (E2: no deliberate attempt by the person; line 17), and two meta-analyses whose subject matter would otherwise fire E5 or E2 (E7, which the screening skill tests first and which stops the sequence). Columns: `record_id, title, year, doi_or_id, expected_decision, expected_code, rationale`. Expected codes follow skills/screening/SKILL.md as revised in this round (E7 tested first, then E1–E5 in order; E8 only for an unopenable full text; E6 is the head agent's deduplication code and is never expected from a screener). The file carries titles and DOIs only; the head agent assembles the screening records file (record_id, title, abstract, year, authors, source_db, doi) from the staged record data, and the screeners decide from the record text alone. The three immune-conditioning decoys are placebo/conditioning records, not A09 immune-challenge studies; if a safety filter stops a run on one of them, the stop is recorded (trace `safety_stop_subject`; methods-paper outcome #8) and the record is replaced from the same reference list at Sean's direction.

## Procedure
1. Screening: both screener agents (A, B) screen the five selected records, the Paravlic 2018 record and the ten decoys at `ta` (16 records), then the five selected records at `ft`. The head agent compares each decision with the expected decision (decoys.csv; the five selected records are expected `include`; Paravlic `exclude`/E7) and the two screeners with each other.
2. Extraction: both extractor agents extract the five studies into separate copies of master_extraction.csv. The head agent diffs them with tools/reconcile.py; discrepancies are listed (tools/RECONCILIATION.md).
3. Appraisal: appraisal agent applies the tool selected from each paper's design statement (appraisal skill mapping; Manuck 1976 and Zeidan 2011 as noted above) to each of the five studies and drafts the GRADE row for each ability. Paravlic 2018 is not appraised.
4. Reviewer: reviewer agent, fresh session, audits the five extractions against the full texts and the targets as confirmed under the precision rule.
5. Pooling-code test (synthetic): `bash analysis/synthetic/run_synthetic_tests.sh` from the package root (fixer B's script; the five dry-run studies inform five different abilities, k = 1 each, so the real dry run never reaches pooling, leave-one-out, Egger, forest or funnel code). The script generates the synthetic masters under analysis/synthetic/ (every `study_id` starts with `synth_`, provenance fields are obviously synthetic, and nothing is written under extraction/), runs `Rscript analysis/run_all.R` on a dry-run-shaped master (five abilities, k = 1) and on a pooling master (k ≥ 3 per unit, one k = 12 unit for Egger and funnel) and asserts the contract outputs and headers. **Pass criterion: exit 0 and the asserted outputs** (the script's final line reads `== synthetic tests: 0 failure(s)`). Checked 2026-10-04 on a copy of this tree in the build environment (R 4.3.3, metafor 4.4.0, bayesmeta absent): exit 0, 51 checks ok, 0 failures; bayes_pooled.csv carries note rows because bayesmeta is absent.
6. Environment: `Rscript analysis/setup.R`; `Rscript analysis/run_all.R` on the reconciled dry-run master (five real studies). Confirm the one-command rebuild and the provenance refusal (delete one location field in a scratch copy and confirm the load stops; analysis/00_load.R writes REFUSED_*.csv).
7. Every run logged with the trace logger; every prompt stored under traces/prompts/.

## Agreement statistics and acceptance
- Screening: Cohen's κ (agent A vs agent B) at `ta` on the 16 records and at `ft` on the five, each **reported with its 95% CI**. At this size κ is reported, not used as the acceptance threshold: with 16 records whose expected split (5 include, 11 exclude) is fixed by construction, the CI of κ is wide, one disagreement moves κ substantially, and the decoys were chosen to be clear-cut, so κ measures the test's design as much as the screeners. **Acceptance criterion: every disagreement (agent vs agent, and agent vs expected decision or expected code) is listed in the dry-run report and adjudicated by Sean, with the reason.** The exclusion code is compared as well as the decision, so that a correct `exclude` with the wrong code (for example E2 or E5 recorded for a meta-analysis instead of E7) is a listed disagreement.
- Extraction: field-level exact-agreement rate and numeric discrepancy rate (tools/reconcile.py); every discrepancy listed and adjudicated.

## Access plan
Full texts are staged by Sean before the run (rule (b)); only Kozhevnikov 2013 (PLoS ONE) is open access with confirmed access today. The research document records these access failures during its own review (line 206), and the dry run expects them: **ahajournals, Wiley, Taylor & Francis, Science and gastrojournal returned 403; PubMed pages returned no content; PNAS, PMC and JAMA Network intermittently served CAPTCHAs; Europe PMC, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and ResearchGate rate-limited after a few requests.** Consequences for the dry run: agents never decide from a snippet (screening rule 5: an unopenable full text is `unsure`/E8 for Sean); API lookups are paced (plan quality control "citation verification with pacing"); each staged full text records its `access_route`; and any new failure is added to this list in the dry-run report (methods-paper outcome #8).

## Pass criteria
- Every printed target reproduced exactly as printed in the paper (precision rule), each with a complete provenance block; every derived target reproduced by analysis/01_effect_sizes.R from the extracted printed inputs, to the research document's precision, with the derivation recorded in `derivation`.
- Extractor A and B agree on every target value, or every discrepancy is explained by a documented source ambiguity and adjudicated.
- Screening: every disagreement listed and adjudicated (κ with CI reported); Paravlic 2018 excluded with E7 by both screeners; no decoy included.
- Each of the four skills executed on at least one real paper, with its trace record complete.
- Reviewer report: no open FAIL on the dry-run package.
- `bash analysis/synthetic/run_synthetic_tests.sh` exits 0 with the asserted outputs.
- run_all.R rebuilds from the reconciled master; renv.lock and session_info.txt committed (environment route per analysis/ENVIRONMENT.md and R-038).
- No agent run touched A09 material.

## Report
dry-run/DRY_RUN_REPORT_<date>.md: selection table with verification routes and the printed figures confirmed under the precision rule; per-study target vs extracted (A, B); κ with CI and the full disagreement list with adjudications; extraction discrepancy list; appraisal rows with the tool-selection rule recorded for each study; reviewer report; synthetic-test output; environment manifest; trace ids; list of what did not work and why (including access failures and any safety stop). This report is the core of gate-packages/G1_<date>_team-and-tooling.md.
